 You can take 44 days of vacation in 2027 with just 11 days of PTO
 If your vacation plans outweigh your PTO allotment, here's how you can quadruple your paid time away from work in 2027 with some strategic planning.
 Unsplash / Christopher Carson 
 Save 
 Share 
 Brianna Perry 
  –  
 Staff Writer
  ·  
 November 19, 2026
 Add us as a preferred source 
 The term “work-life balance” is pretty much nonexistent in a New Yorker’s vocabulary, especially when our paid time off seems to vanish quicker than a poolside daiquiri. To make matters worse, American workers aren’t exactly swimming in paid vacation days, with the average employee receiving just 10 to 11 days a year But here’s the silver lining: there are ways to double, triple, and even quadruple your vacation days. All it takes is a bit of strategic planning.
 The trick is to plan your time off around existing federal holidays and long weekends , giving yourself longer breaks without burning through your entire PTO balance.

 Whether you’re eyeing a quick escape from the concrete jungle or plotting a full blown international getaway, here’s how to turn your limited PTO into as much time off as possible in 2027. 
 2027 National Holiday Calendar
 Maximizing your PTO all starts with knowing when the built-in days off already exist. 
 Here’s a full look at the 2027 U.S. federal holiday calendar: 
 🎊 New Year’s Day –  Friday, January 1, 2027
 🖤 Martin Luther King Jr. Day –  Monday, January 18, 2027
 🏛 Presidents’ Day –  Monday, February 15, 2027
 🇺🇲 Memorial Day –  Monday, May 31, 2027
 ✊🏿 Juneteenth –  Saturday, June 19, 2027 (Observed Friday, June 18) 
 🎆 Independence Day – Sunday, July 4, 2027 (Observed Monday, July 5) 
 ⚒️️ Labor Day –  Monday, September 6, 2027
 🧡 Indigenous Peoples’ Day –  Monday, October 11, 2027
 🎖 Veteran’s Day –  Thursday, November 11, 2027
 🦃 Thanksgiving – Thursday, November 25, 2027
 🎄 Christmas Day –  Saturday, December 25, 2027 (Observed Friday, December 24) 
 By strategically lining up your PTO with existing holidays and weekends, you can turn just a few days away from work into several extended breaks throughout 2027.
 Shutterstock / xtock 
 How to turn 11 PTO days into 44 days off in 2027
 By taking just one PTO day next to each of the 11 federal holidays, you can turn them into 11 separate four-day weekends throughout the year.
 January 4th, 2027 – supplemented by New Year’s Day and the preceding weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 January 19th, 2027 – supplemented by the preceding weekend and Martin Luther King Jr. Day for 4 consecutive days off
 February 16th, 2027 – supplemented by the preceding weekend and Presidents’ Day for 4 consecutive days off
 June 1st, 2027 – supplemented by Memorial Day and the preceding weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 June 21st, 2027 – supplemented by Juneteenth and the preceding weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 July 6th, 2027 – supplemented by Independence Day and the preceding weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 September 7th, 2027 – supplemented by Labor Day and the preceding weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 October 12th, 2027 – supplemented by Columbus Day and the preceding weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 November 12th, 2027 – supplemented by Veterans Day and the following weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 November 26th, 2027 – supplemented by Thanksgiving and the following weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 December 27th, 2027 – supplemented by Christmas Day and the preceding weekend for 4 consecutive days off
 With that being said, this isn’t the only option for maximizing your PTO in 2027.
 Unsplash / Safwan Mahmud 
 How to use your PTO for 9 or 10 consecutive days off in 2027
 If you’re looking for a longer getaway rather than several mini vacations, these are the dates to circle on your 2027 calendar:
 December 28th–31st, 2026 – supplemented by Christmas Day, New Year’s Day, and the weekends on either side for 10 consecutive days off (December 25th, 2026–January 3rd, 2027)
 January 19th–22nd, 2027 – supplemented by Martin Luther King Jr. Day and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (January 16th–24th)
 February 16th–19th, 2027 – supplemented by Presidents’ Day and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (February 13th–21st)
 June 1st–4th, 2027 – supplemented by Memorial Day and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (May 29th–June 6th)
 June 14th–17th, 2027 – supplemented by Juneteenth and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (June 12th–20th)
 July 6th–9th, 2027 – supplemented by Independence Day and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (July 3rd–11th)
 September 7th–10th, 2027 – supplemented by Labor Day and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (September 4th–12th)
 October 12th–15th, 2027 – supplemented by Columbus Day and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (October 9th–17th)
 November 8th–10th and 12th, 2027 – supplemented by Veterans Day and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (November 6th–14th)
 November 22nd–24th and 26th, 2027 – supplemented by Thanksgiving and the weekends on either side for 9 consecutive days off (November 20th–28th)
 December 27th–30th, 2027 – supplemented by Christmas Day and New Year’s Day 2028, plus the weekends on either side, for 10 consecutive days off (December 24th, 2027–January 2nd, 2028)
 Of course, be sure to check your company’s holiday schedule before booking those flights–not every employer observes all federal holidays. Otherwise, if you’ve been waiting for a sign to finally book that big trip, consider this your excuse to start planning!
